name: Borosil Renewables Ltd
tagline: India's only large-scale low-iron solar-glass maker - now four straight quarters of >33% EBITDA margin, rising ASPs and a swing back to profit, powered by an import-protection stack (ADD + CVD + ALMM List-II) and a 60% capacity expansion commissioning Q4 FY27; the offset is that the margin is policy-boosted and above through-cycle
business_overview: Borosil Renewables manufactures low-iron textured solar glass, holding over 15% of the Indian market and positioned as the world's largest solar glass producer outside China - a direct beneficiary of India's utility-scale and rooftop solar capacity additions and of the ALMM List-II domestic-content mandate.

fundamentals_narrative: The 'ROE 12%, choppy earnings' picture from the prior pass is stale. Borosil has now printed four consecutive quarters with EBITDA margin above 33% (35% in Q1 FY27), swung from a Rs 203 Cr net loss in Q1 FY26 to a Rs 87 Cr net profit, and pushed average ex-factory selling price to Rs 160.3/sq.mm from Rs 138.1 a year ago (Rs 150.2 the prior quarter). The drivers are an import-protection stack - anti-dumping duty on Chinese/Vietnamese solar glass (Dec 2024, five years), countervailing duty on Malaysian glass (Jun 2026), and the ALMM List-II domestic-content mandate (Jun 2026) - plus the clean exit of the chronically loss-making European (GMB/Interfloat) business. A 600 TPD expansion (SG-4/SG-5, Rs 950 Cr) is on track for Q4 FY27 commissioning, adding ~60% volume into FY28, and management targets Rs 4,000 Cr+ revenue within 3-4 years. Debt is modest and the expansion is largely warrant-funded. The central caveat: 35% EBITDA margin is well above the through-cycle level (historical ROE ~12%), the uplift is policy- and supply-gap-driven, and domestic solar-glass capacity is being added rapidly across the industry (toward 7,700 TPD by Mar-27).

Solar glass is a commodity where Chinese producers (Xinyi, Flat Glass) hold a structural cost advantage absent protection
Demand is cyclical and tied to the pace of Indian solar installations and module localisation
Rs 950 Cr expansion means negative free-cash conversion through the ramp; industry-wide capacity additions raise late-cycle glut risk
No forum or trusted-user conviction; no dividend track record
verdict_headline: A confirmed four-quarter earnings inflection in a policy-protected market with a 60% capacity expansion landing FY28 - four-box score 2.5, thesis_fit 10x-in-2-3-years on the un-ignorable-growth carve-out with conviction capped at Medium (unconfirmed) given policy-boosted margins
verdict_reasoning: The prior 'Neither cleanly' call is superseded: four consecutive quarters of >33% EBITDA margin, a swing from a Rs 203 Cr loss to a Rs 87 Cr profit, and three rising ASP readings are a real, multi-quarter inflection with a dated catalyst (SG-4/SG-5, 60% volume, Q4 FY27)

four_box score is 2.5 (tailwind yes / tam weak / moat weak / valuation weak). Written exception per the decision table: the earnings inflection is un-ignorable (phreak's carve-out) - loss to sustained strong profit across four quarters - so the 10x-in-2-3-years label is allowed, but conviction caps at Medium with an 'unconfirmed' caveat

The reason for the cap: 35% EBITDA margin sits far above the historical through-cycle level, the uplift is policy-driven (ADD to 2029) and supply-gap-driven, and the whole industry is adding solar-glass capacity - peak_margin_risk is true

Conviction Low-Medium -> Medium: the confirmed inflection, pricing power, protected market, modest debt and funded expansion justify one notch up; policy dependence, the 2029 ADD cliff, commodity economics and negative FCF through the ramp cap it there. No red flag; no trusted floor. Re-check after SG-4/SG-5 commissioning and once a post-expansion margin print is available

track_record.note: FY24-FY26 verifiable. None cleared both revenue growth >=10% and ROCE >=15% in the same year: FY24-FY25 were a Chinese-dumping trough (weak volumes, losses/negligible ROCE), and FY26 - though recovering as the ADD took effect from Dec 2024 - still had a first half that held full-year ROCE below 15%. This is a policy-driven cyclical upturn, not a Coffee-Can consistency record; FY27 could be the first clearing year. Not a young company, so the zero is informative rather than a penalty artefact.

four_box.note: India solar buildout + ALMM localisation + import protection is a genuine multi-year tailwind: yes. Domestic supply gap and a Rs 4,000 Cr revenue ambition give real headroom, but a 10x off a ~Rs 7,350 Cr cap is a stretch: tam weak. >15% domestic share and only-large-scale-maker status plus ALMM demand are edges, but the margin rests on time-limited policy (ADD to 2029) not a structural cost advantage over China: moat weak. ~20x P/E on a policy-inflated, above-through-cycle margin with peak_margin_risk: valuation weak. Score 2.5 -> thesis_fit neither UNLESS a written exception; the un-ignorable multi-quarter earnings inflection (loss to sustained strong profit) qualifies (phreak carve-out), so 10x-in-2-3-years is allowed with conviction capped at Medium (unconfirmed).
